accepted.sentence: With standard right-handed threads, turning clockwise usually tightens a fastener, while turning counterclockwise loosens it.
A longer handle gives the hand more leverage, helping turn a fastener that resists movement.
In a cramped spot, short turns with repeated grip adjustments can advance a fastener where a full rotation is impossible.
For delicate assembly, users make small turns and check how firmly the fastener is seated before continuing.
When a fastener becomes flush with the surface, users stop turning to avoid driving it too deeply.
A pilot hole in wood can guide a fastener and reduce the chance of splitting as it is driven.
To loosen a stuck fastener, a brief push in the tightening direction may help break its resistance before reversal.
After removing a fastener, users lift it clear of the workpiece once its threads have disengaged.
